full_text_zh:
[P1] 童读·中华经典神话故事
混沌凿窍
毛红艳/改编 鸽子插画工作室/绘
新疆人民出版社
新疆青少年出版社

[P2] 中华经典神话故事绘本
混沌凿窍
毛红艳/改编  鸽子插画工作室/绘
新疆人民出版社
新疆科学技术出版社

[P3] 嗨，你好！
我叫倏，是南海大帝。
“倏——倏——倏——”千万别
叫成“嗖——嗖——嗖——”，虽然我
们都跑得像风一样快。

[P4] 这是我的好朋友，他叫“忽”，是北海大帝。
“忽——忽——忽——”千万别当成“呼——
呼——呼——”，他可从来不打呼噜。
我们合体，就是“倏忽”，跑得比风更快，就
像流星划过天空。

[P5] 在南海和北海中间，有巍峨的高山，
广阔的草原，茂密的森林，会吃人的沼泽，这片土地的大帝，名叫混沌。
每年春天，我和忽分别从南海和北海出发，穿过高山、草原、森林和沼泽，
在混沌大帝的宫殿相见。

[P6] “倏，一年不见，你长高了！”
“忽，你的脚怎么比我的大这么多！”
“走，我们和马比一比，看谁跑得快！”
“比就比，和忽在一起，跑一天也不累！”

[P7] 混沌大帝知道我和忽来了，带着我们到处游玩。
第一天，混沌带我们来到草原。
我和忽在草地上打滚儿、倒立、翻跟头，呼呼呼，
从草原这头儿，跑到草原那头儿。
混沌没有眼睛，看不见，“咕咚”，一头扎进了烂泥坑。

[P8] 第二天，混沌带我们来到森林。
我和忽爬到树上，看猴子“喀嚓喀嚓”啃桃子，瞧小鹿“呦呦呦呦”吃绿草，听黄鸟“叽叽叽叽”唱歌谣……
混沌没有耳朵，听不见，他向小溪里扔了一块石头，
“扑通——扑通——”吓得猴子荡上了树梢，惊得小鹿躲进了草丛，黄鸟扑腾着翅膀，瞧不见影儿了。

[P9] 第三天，混沌带我们去看花。
我和忽东闻闻，西嗅嗅，跟着花香
往前走，一溜烟儿钻进了花丛捉迷藏。
混沌没有鼻子，闻不到花香，还在
绕着圈子找花园呢。

[P10] 第四天，混沌带我们摘果子。
桑葚甜滋滋，桃子嘎嘣脆，梅子酸溜溜。
“啊——呸！”什么又苦又涩？原来李子还没熟。
可惜，混沌没有嘴巴，酸甜苦辣甘辛咸，他一样都尝不到。

[P11] “倏，你玩得高兴吗？”“我很高兴呀！”
“可是混沌看不见，听不见，吃不到，闻不到，肯定很不开心！我们能不能都帮他呢？”
“我们有眼睛、耳朵、鼻子、嘴巴，叫做七窍，所以能看美景、听声音、闻气味、吃美食，要不，我们也给混沌凿出七窍吧？”

[P12] 第一天和第二天，我们给混沌凿出了一双圆溜溜的大眼睛。这双眼睛上下左右滴溜溜乱转，看见什么都觉得新奇。
第三天和第四天，我们给混沌凿出了一双尖尖的耳朵。这双耳朵听我们讲故事，连眼睛跟着一起笑。

[P13] 第五天，我们给混沌凿出了一个高高的鼻子。这个鼻子闻到了味道，就会“嘶嘶嘶”吸个不停，好像要把所有的香味都吸进鼻子里。
第六天和第七天，我们给混沌凿出了一张微笑的嘴巴。可是，这张嘴巴却不会在听到好玩的故事时哈哈大笑，看见可怕的虫子时哇哇大叫。

[P14] 混沌没有了呼吸，他再也不能和我们一起去草原和森林，一起看花、摘果。
他跟我和忽一样，有了圆溜溜的大眼睛、尖尖的耳朵、高高的鼻子、微笑的嘴巴，却失去了生命。
混沌静静地躺着，就像在做一个长长的没有尽头的美梦。

[P15] 小草悄悄地，悄悄地爬满了混沌的身体。
野花从小草中间钻出来，像星星一样美丽。

[P16] 种子飞快地发芽，抽枝，开花，结出香甜的果子。
黄鸟落在果树上，唱着动听的歌谣。

[P17] 原来，青草绿，野花香，果子甜，
鸟儿鸣，都藏在混沌的心里。
full_text_en:
[P1] Children's Reading · Chinese Classic Mythological Stories
Hun Dun and the Opening of the Orifices
Adapted by Mao Hongyan, Illustrated by Pigeon Illustration Studio
Xinjiang People's Publishing House
Xinjiang Youth and Children's Publishing House

[P2] Chinese Classic Mythological Story Picture Book
Hun Dun Carving the Aperture
Adapted by Mao Hongyan  Illustrated by Pigeon Illustration Studio
Xinjiang People's Publishing House
Xinjiang Science and Technology Press

[P3] Hi, hello!
I'm Shu, the Emperor of the South Sea.
"Shu——Shu——Shu——" Don't ever
say "Soo——Soo——Soo——", even though
we all run as fast as the wind.

[P4] This is my good friend. His name is 'Hu', the Lord of the Northern Sea.
'Hu—hu—hu—' — don't mistake it for 'Hu—hu—hu—' like snoring. He never snores.
When we combine, we become 'Shu Hu', running faster than the wind, like a meteor streaking across the sky.

[P5] In the middle of the South Sea and the North Sea, there are towering mountains,
boundless grasslands, dense forests, and marshes that eat people. The great emperor of this land is called Hun沌.
Every spring, my friend Hu and I set out from the South Sea and the North Sea, crossing mountains, grasslands, forests, and marshes,
to meet at the palace of Emperor Hun沌.

[P6] "Shu, it's been a year, you've grown taller!"
"Hu, why are your feet so much bigger than mine!"
"Come on, let's race a horse and see who's faster!"
"Let's race, running with Hu, I won't get tired even after a whole day!"

[P7] The Chaos Emperor knew I and Hu had arrived, and took us to play everywhere.
On the first day, Chaos took us to the grassland.
I and Hu rolled around, did handstands, and cartwheels on the grass, huffing and puffing,
running from one end of the grassland to the other.
Chaos had no eyes, couldn't see, and with a 'gurgle', plunged headfirst into a muddy pit.

[P8] The next day, Chaos took us to the forest.
I and Hu climbed up a tree, watching monkeys 'crunch crunch' eating peaches, seeing little deer 'bleat bleat bleat' eating green grass, and listening to yellow birds 'chirp chirp chirp' singing songs...
Chaos had no ears and couldn't hear. He threw a stone into the stream,
'Plop—plop—' scaring the monkey onto the treetop, startling the deer into the grass, and making the yellow bird flap its wings and disappear from sight.

[P9] On the third day, Chaos took us to see flowers.
I and Hu sniffed here and there, following the scent of flowers,
and in a flash, we darted into the flower bushes to play hide-and-seek.
Chaos has no nose, can't smell the flowers, and is still
wandering in circles looking for the garden.

[P10] On the fourth day, Hun Dun took us to pick fruits.
Mulberries are sweet and juicy, peaches are crisp, and plums are sour.
"Ah—pah!" What's bitter and sour? Oh, the plums aren't ripe yet.
Too bad, Hun Dun has no mouth—he can't taste sweet, sour, bitter, spicy, salty, or umami at all.

[P11] "Shu, are you having fun?" "I'm having a great time!"
"But Chaos can't see, can't hear, can't eat, can't smell — he must be very unhappy! Can we help him?"
"We have eyes, ears, nose, and mouth — called the seven orifices — so we can see beautiful scenery, hear sounds, smell scents, and enjoy delicious food. What if we also carve seven orifices for Chaos?"

[P12] On the first and second days, we carved a pair of round, big eyes for Hun沌. These eyes spun up, down, left, and right, finding everything new and fascinating.
On the third and fourth days, we carved a pair of pointed ears for Hun沌. These ears listened to us tell stories, and even the eyes followed along, laughing together.

[P13] On the fifth day, we carved a tall nose for Hun沌. This nose, when it smelled something, would 'ssss' suck continuously, as if trying to draw in all the fragrances into its nostrils.
On the sixth and seventh days, we carved a smiling mouth for Hun沌. But this mouth couldn't laugh heartily at funny stories, nor cry out in fear when seeing scary bugs.

[P14] Hundun had no breath left; he could no longer go with us to the grasslands and forests, to see flowers and pick fruits.
He was just like me and Hu, with big round eyes, pointed ears, a tall nose, and a smiling mouth, yet he had lost his life.
Hundun lay quietly, as if dreaming a long, endless beautiful dream.

[P15] The little grass quietly, quietly crept over Hun Dun's body.
Wildflowers emerged from between the grass, beautiful like stars.

[P16] The seed quickly sprouted, grew branches, bloomed, and bore sweet fruits.
The yellow bird perched on the fruit tree, singing a pleasant melody.

[P17] Originally, the green grass, fragrant wildflowers, sweet fruits,
and singing birds were all hidden within混沌's heart.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《混沌凿窍》的封面，展示了书名、作者、插画师及出版社信息，画面中央是一个长着翅膀的橙色圆胖生物，头顶停着一只彩色小鸟，背景是花草和树枝。
[P2] 本页为绘本《混沌凿窍》的封面，展示了书名、作者、插画师及出版社信息，画面中央是一个长着翅膀的橙色圆胖生物，两侧有两位长着翅膀和鱼尾的女性角色，背景是云朵和波浪。
[P3] 画面中，南海大帝倏从云中浮现，向读者自我介绍，并强调自己的名字是“倏”而非“嗖”，同时说明他们跑得像风一样快。背景是云海、山峦和游动的鱼形生物。
[P4] 南海大帝倏介绍他的好朋友北海大帝忽，强调其名字读音，并说明两人合体后速度极快，如同流星划过天空。
[P5] 本页描绘了南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽每年春天从各自海域出发，穿越高山、草原、森林和沼泽，前往混沌大帝宫殿相会的场景，文字介绍了混沌统治的地域和两位大帝的会面传统。
[P6] 南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽在山间相遇，互相打趣对方的外貌变化，并决定与马赛跑，展现他们亲密无间、充满活力的友谊。
[P7] 混沌大帝带南海大帝倏和北海大帝忽在草原上玩耍，他们尽情打滚、奔跑，而混沌因没有眼睛不慎跌入泥坑。
[P8] 混沌带南海大帝倏和北海大帝忽来到森林，他们观察动物，混沌因没有耳朵，扔石头后吓跑了森林里的猴子、小鹿和黄鸟。
[P9] 混沌带南海大帝倏和北海大帝忽去赏花，两人在花丛中捉迷藏，而混沌因没有鼻子闻不到花香，仍在原地绕圈寻找花园。
[P10] 混沌带南海大帝倏和北海大帝忽摘果子，两人品尝了桑葚、桃子和梅子，而混沌因没有嘴巴无法品尝任何味道，只能看着李子未熟而遗憾。
[P11] 南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽在玩耍后，讨论混沌因缺少五官而无法感受世界，决定为混沌凿出七窍，以帮助他体验感官之乐。
[P12] 南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽为混沌凿出眼睛和耳朵，混沌开始用新感官体验世界，眼睛转动观察，耳朵聆听故事并随之发笑。
[P13] 南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽为混沌凿出鼻子和嘴巴，但混沌的鼻子只会不停吸气，嘴巴却无法表达喜怒哀乐。
[P14] 混沌在被凿出七窍后失去了呼吸和生命，静静躺着，仿佛在做一场无尽的美梦，南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽在一旁悲伤地守护着他。
[P15] 混沌静卧于草地上，小草和野花悄然覆盖了他的身体，画面宁静而美丽。
[P16] 画面描绘了种子发芽、开花结果的生机景象，黄鸟在果树上歌唱，而混沌则在云雾中安睡，仿佛与自然融为一体。
[P17] 画面描绘混沌在花草丛中欢快奔跑，周围鸟语花香，生机盎然，文字点明自然的美好感受其实一直存在于混沌的内心。
[P18] 画面中，混沌被南海大帝倏与北海大帝忽环绕，两人似乎在守护或陪伴着他，混沌面带平静表情，周围有云雾缭绕，整体氛围宁静而充满神秘感。
